title: Integral and field tensor inverses on a pure-dimensional smooth clopen component
statement: Fix the purity coefficient datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the fixed algebraic closure [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $X_i$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $j:X_i\to X$ an open and closed immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Fix any normalized all-coefficients exceptional comparison record $R$ for $(g,c,j)$ [def-pur-clopen-exceptional-all-coefficients], and assume that $g\circ j$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf N$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the tensor products and coefficient units of [def-pur-clopen-coefficient-operations] and the finite-Tor predicates of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then the actual component integral exceptional image $\omega=R.\mathrm{integralI}(\mathcal O_{E,Y})$ and a two-sided tensor inverse $Q$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(X_i,\mathcal O_E)$, with isomorphisms $\omega\otimes Q\simeq\mathcal O_{E,X_i}$ and $Q\otimes\omega\simeq\mathcal O_{E,X_i}$. Likewise the actual component rational exceptional image $R.\mathrm{rationalI}(E_Y)$ has a two-sided inverse in its rational constructible category. For every finite coefficient stage $A$ of the fixed algebraic closure, the actual component common-stage exceptional image $R.\mathrm{actionI}(\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Y}[A])$ has a two-sided inverse for the specified common-stage tensor, with target the unit represented at $A$. These are three existence assertions about a single pure-dimensional component, with no finite partition, global assembly, or prescribed component maps. The empty source and $d=0$ are included, and no Tate orientation or trivialization is chosen.

proof.text: Finite-type geometry and the coefficient hypotheses apply to X_i and Y, without absolute separatedness. Compare R.base.integralI to the normalized integral exceptional functor for c.precomp j by the unique counit-preserving comparison of right adjoints to the very same specified integral compact-support functor. Their unit values are isomorphic, so their scalar reductions are isomorphic. Use the normalized integral exceptional construction and its actual reduction system to identify its residue with the finite exceptional image of the coefficient unit; this is not an inference from equality of arbitrary tower limits. Smooth tensor duality for g composed with j gives an etale rank-one line L shifted by 2d. The finite exceptional adjunction and intrinsic site realization identify that finite exceptional image with the intrinsic pullback of L[2d]. Transport this presentation to the residue of the actual R.base.integralI unit value through the reduction of the integral right-adjoint comparison. The latter integral object is derived complete because it belongs to the integral constructible category.

source.place: First paragraph, shifted rank-one smooth dualizing object; integral and field extension in Step 4 of finite-clopen inverse assembly

proof.text: Apply the complete-residue-line inverse theorem with m=2d to this complete object. It gives its internal-Hom dual, both specified completed-tensor evaluation isomorphisms, constructibility, and common Tor intervals [-2d,-2d] and [2d,2d] at all positive reductions. Regard the dual as an object of the full integral constructible category, and lift both evaluations through the fully faithful inclusion. The tensor and unit are the same normalized completed operations defining the clopen tensor and unit, so these lifted maps are exactly the two required inverse isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply rational localization to that pair and its evaluation isomorphisms. On integral representatives the rational tensor is the same tensor and its unit is the image of the same integral unit. The rationalObjectI coherence field of R identifies the exceptional factor with the specified rational exceptional image. This gives the rational assertion. For a coefficient stage A repeat the integral argument with R.stage A and localize there; the stage_eqI field identifies that rational exceptional functor with the stage of R.actionI. Represent the inverse and both arrows at A. The normalized common-stage tensor and unit comparisons identify their sources and targets, including the identity-extension case. Functoriality preserves both inverse identities. Empty components have zero coefficient categories, so every map is the unique isomorphism and the same bounds are valid.

theorem smooth_clopen_component_inverse
    (Xi : Over (Spec (.of P.field.k)))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Xi.left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Xi.left ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (c : Compactification g) (j : Xi ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j.left] [IsClosedImmersion j.left]
    (R : ClopenExceptionalAllCoefficients P X Y Xi g c j)
    (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (j.left ≫ g)] :
    (let omega := R.base.integralI.obj (P.clopenIntegralUnit Y.left)
     finiteTorConstructibleIntegral P.coefficients.l P.extension Xi.left omega.obj ∧
       ∃ Q, finiteTorConstructibleIntegral P.coefficients.l P.extension Xi.left Q.obj ∧
         Nonempty ((P.clopenIntegralTensor Xi).obj (omega, Q) ≅
           P.clopenIntegralUnit Xi.left) ∧
         Nonempty ((P.clopenIntegralTensor Xi).obj (Q, omega) ≅
           P.clopenIntegralUnit Xi.left)) ∧
    (let omega := R.base.rationalI.obj (P.clopenRationalUnit Y.left)
     ∃ Q, Nonempty ((P.clopenRationalTensor Xi).obj (omega, Q) ≅
         P.clopenRationalUnit Xi.left) ∧
       Nonempty ((P.clopenRationalTensor Xi).obj (Q, omega) ≅
         P.clopenRationalUnit Xi.left)) ∧
    (∀ A : AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Index P.coefficients.l P.coefficients.Qbar,
     let omega := R.actionI.functor.obj (P.clopenCommonStageUnit Y.left A)
     ∃ Q, Nonempty ((P.clopenCommonStageTensor Xi).obj (omega, Q) ≅
         P.clopenCommonStageUnit Xi.left A) ∧
       Nonempty ((P.clopenCommonStageTensor Xi).obj (Q, omega) ≅
         P.clopenCommonStageUnit Xi.left A))

The generic bounded-below etale/pro-etale comparison identifies the actual finite exceptional unit image with the intrinsic image of the shifted line.
Uniqueness compares an arbitrary record integralI functor with the canonical normalized integral exceptional functor before using its canonical finite reductions.
